decisions.statement: A log day is kept seven days where no other window is stated.
A day's date is read off one property line of its page's text rather than by loading the page.
A page whose date cannot be read from its text is left as that page is.
A page left that way is counted and named.
The removal is composed by a daemon rather than authored.
The removal lands mechanically in process and owes no read record.
The lines beside a page go with a plain remove after that page has landed.
The reading kept over a page's path goes with the page.
The days go in one call to land in one commit.
A day is tried alone where that call refuses.
Every day still there after a refusal is named.
Nothing is taken away unless the sweep is asked to.
The days are what the index answers rather than a folder listed.

definition: every log day past the window a log is kept for taken away
